newsitem.title: USA: New Brunswick's 630 MW nuke resumes full output.
newsitem.headline: New Brunswick's 630 MW nuke resumes full output.

text.p: New Brunswick Power Corp said its 630 megawatt (MW) Point Lepreau nuclear power station resumed full operation over the weekend following repairs to its boiler tubes.
"We're back at full power now. We're back on line a little earlier than expected," said a company spokesman.
The plant was set to return to service in early November.
During the outage, begun in late September, crews examined the boiler instrumentation and replaced eroded pipes inside the plant's four boilers.
The Lepreau nuclear station, 45 kilometers south of the city of St John, was scheduled to shut in April 1997 for maintenance, the spokesman said.
Headquartered in Frederiction, New Brunswick Power's installed capacity totals 4,000 MW.
